cold_solve.method: Passage + stem + options read first; every option argued FOR in turn before any option was rejected; the rationale and generator_meta were read only after the answer was fixed.
cold_solve.argued_for_A: A = 'It sheltered the battens from the weather, so the timber under old roofs usually stayed sound.' Best case for A: the passage does credit torching with stopping wind-driven ingress ('it was there to stop the fine snow, dust and draughts that wind pushes up between the tiles. At that job it worked'), and that ingress would otherwise land in the batten zone, so 'sheltered the battens' is not absurd on its face. REJECTED on two independent grounds. (1) The second clause is flatly contradicted by the anchor: 'whatever wet reached the torching sat against the battens until they decayed along its line' - the timber did NOT stay sound, it decayed, and decayed specifically where the torching ran. (2) The passage assigns 'the sheltering' by name to a different component in its last sentence: 'Felt under the battens does the sheltering now.' A borrows that verb from the felt. A is the reversed mechanism.
cold_solve.argued_for_B: B = 'It was what held the unnailed courses of tiles in place once they had been hung.' Best case for B: the mortar is described as 'pressed up against the backs of the tiles from inside', which is physically a bond surface, and the passage does volunteer that only 'every fourth course' is nailed - so it explicitly raises the question of what holds the other three courses. REJECTED. The passage answers that question itself, and not with mortar: 'The tiles themselves hang from two small lugs at the head, the nibs, hooked over each batten.' The nibs carry the unnailed courses. The ordering seals it: 'It went on after the tiles were hung' - the roof was already holding itself up before any torching existed. And the stem is 'What are we told about torching?', so a holding role that is nowhere stated fails the stem even before it is contradicted.
cold_solve.argued_for_C: C = 'It made the loft weathertight the year round, whatever the weather drove against the roof.' Best case for C: this is the option closest to a fair summary of the concession sentence 'At that job it worked', and 'weathertight' is a reasonable gloss on stopping snow, dust and draughts. REJECTED. The job is enumerated and narrow - fine snow, dust and draughts 'that wind pushes up between the tiles', i.e. wind-driven ingress - and 'At that job' explicitly restricts the endorsement to that enumerated job. The anchor then presupposes the opposite of weathertightness: 'whatever wet reached the torching' concedes that liquid water got past the tiles to the mortar. C is a scope upgrade over an explicitly bounded claim.
cold_solve.argued_for_D: D = 'It held the wet it took up against the battens, and the wood rotted there.' The anchor states it once: 'But mortar that touches timber passes damp to it, and whatever wet reached the torching sat against the battens until they decayed along its line.' D recasts that in different words - the mortar kept the water it received in contact with the battens ('sat against the battens' -> 'held ... against the battens'), and the timber rotted at that contact ('they decayed along its line' -> 'the wood rotted there'). Every element of D has a licensing element in the anchor. ACCEPTED.
cold_solve.uniqueness: Exactly one defensible answer. A is falsified twice, B is both unstated and contradicted by the nibs sentence and by the ordering, C is falsified by the bounded 'At that job' and by 'whatever wet reached the torching'. D is uniquely text-supported. The design claim that lay intuition lands on A and B is correct as far as it goes - mortar-as-protection and mortar-as-adhesive are the two lay priors, and the passage refutes both explicitly - but see finding N1: the real-world literature is a three-way split, not a one-way pull.
cold_solve.agrees_with_gkey_legs: Both batch18 G-KEY records (verdicts.jsonl, votes 1 and 2, executed_by claude-fable-5/G-KEY-A and /G-KEY-B) independently solve D and both quote the same anchor sentence. 2 records, 0 kills, 0 flags. My cold solve was reached independently and lands on the same sentence.
cold_solve.residual_on_the_key: One word in D is looser than the rationale's claim that D 'adds nothing the text does not supply': 'the wet it took up' asserts uptake/absorption by the mortar, which the passage implies ('mortar that touches timber passes damp to it') but never states. See finding N5. It does not create a second defensible answer and does not unseat D.

findings.claim: generator_meta.mechanism_verification_note presents SIX quoted strings as coming from one named document - the Wienerberger technical note 'Dr John notes: Torching' (wienerberger.co.uk PDF), which it calls 'the decisive source for this item's direction'. Two of the six are NOT in that document.
findings.evidence: This audit fetched the exact PDF the note names and extracted its full text with pdftotext. Present verbatim: 'because of the risk of water ingress due to capillary attraction caused by the torching material'; 'The fact that the torching comes into contact with the timber battens, hence introducing dampness and eventual decay, goes against all current roof tiling practice and indeed British Standards'; 'Torching was applied in the past to prevent draughts and keep out driving rain'; 'In modern roofing these functions are performed by the underlay'. ABSENT: the note's 'a mixture of lime mortar and horsehair' - the PDF instead reads "Traditionally, this was done using a hair/lime/Portland cement mortar mix", and the string 'horsehair' does not occur anywhere in the document. ABSENT: 'the practice largely became outdated in the late 1930s when bitumen underfelt was used more extensively' - the PDF says nothing about the 1930s, underfelt, or when the practice ended. The document is 26 lines long; there is nowhere for the sentences to hide.
findings.why: Metadata-only, and the underlying FACTS both hold at sources this audit located and verified: jdbsurveys.com/what-is-roof-mortar-torching/ carries 'This is a mixture of lime mortar and horsehair' and 'The practice became outdated in the late 1930s as bitumen under-felt began to be used instead'. So the passage's horsehair and its pre-1930s/felt-displacement arc are correctly grounded - they are simply grounded somewhere other than where the note says. No student-facing text is wrong and no answer design depends on the attribution. The four quotes that DO reproduce are the ones carrying the item's whole directional claim (damp to the battens, eventual decay, purpose, displacement), so the note's central assertion - that this PDF is the decisive source for the item's direction - is TRUE. Recorded because a verification note whose value is that it is checkable must be checkable line by line, and two of its lines fail the check. The fix is one sentence of re-attribution, not a text change.

findings.stage_challenged: gate-disposition: the live G-STEM WORLD_KNOWLEDGE major (with an evidence-backed mitigation this audit found)
findings.claim: DISPOSITION LINE, offered because none exists. verdicts.jsonl carries G-STEM verdict 'flag', blind_classification WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, blind_pick D, at gate severity major, undischarged by any text edit and live in the shipping unit; batch18 has no ASSEMBLY.md and no reviews/pedagogy or reviews/integrated record for this unit at audit time, so the flag is carried with no disposition anywhere. SEPARATELY: this audit's source work materially WEAKENS the flag's premise.
findings.evidence: The flag reads: 'Building-conservation knowledge decides this: lime torching is documented as taking up and holding moisture against the roof battens, causing batten decay, so a reader who knows the practice picks D with no text.' That premise assumes the domain has one settled account. It does not. This audit fetched three real sources and they point three different ways. (a) Wienerberger/Sandtoft 'Dr John notes: Torching' - 'the torching comes into contact with the timber battens, hence introducing dampness and eventual decay' - supports D. (b) theyorkshirelime.company/the-importance-of-lime-torching/ - 'Lime mortar is vapour-permeable. This means it allows trapped moisture within the roof space to evaporate naturally' and 'In older properties without modern ventilation systems, this helps prevent condensation and timber decay' - a live conservation position that supports something close to A, i.e. torching as the battens' protector. (c) buildingconservation.com 'Clay-tiled Roofs' - 'Lime mortar, sometimes with straw and other aggregates, would often be applied to the internal face of the tiles to fill the gaps and help improve the general fixing of the tile' - a conservation source explicitly crediting torching with helping FIX the tiles, which is substantive real-world support for distractor B, the option the unit's own notes dismiss as 'the commonest lay belief'.
findings.why: A domain reader does not reliably arrive at D. A reader schooled on manufacturer technical notes and British Standards does; a reader schooled on lime-conservation advocacy is pulled toward A; a reader who has read buildingconservation.com on plain tiling has textual warrant for B. That is three defensible world-knowledge routes for four options, which is close to the ideal case for a WORLD_KNOWLEDGE flag - the domain does not decide the item, the passage does. The gate itself declined to kill on the neighbouring ground that A and B remain substantive competing claims; this audit's evidence strengthens that ground rather than merely asserting it. DISPOSITION: accept the flag as recorded, at note severity, on the finding that the domain literature is genuinely three-way split and therefore confers no reliable shortcut. No text change is owed and none would help - the counterintuitive mechanism IS the item.

findings.stage_challenged: structural leak - this audit's own hunt; a residue no gate leg named
findings.claim: 3-vs-1 VALENCE SPLIT. Across the four options, A, B and C each credit torching with a beneficial function (it sheltered / it held / it made weathertight); D alone attributes harm (it held wet against the battens and the wood rotted). The key is the sole odd one out on a valence axis that is visible from the option set alone, with no passage.
findings.evidence: Option texts as shipped: A 'It sheltered the battens from the weather, so the timber under old roofs usually stayed sound.' B 'It was what held the unnailed courses of tiles in place once they had been hung.' C 'It made the loft weathertight the year round, whatever the weather drove against the roof.' D 'It held the wet it took up against the battens, and the wood rotted there.' A/B/C are three different functions but one valence; D is the only failure claim. This is a different axis from the two G-STEM findings (world knowledge; absolutiser strip) and neither leg names it.
findings.why: Recorded as a SOFT lean, not a decided answer. 'Pick the option that stands apart from a cluster' is a real test-wiseness heuristic, and it compounds with the undisputed absolutiser strip: strike C on form, then take the odd one out of the remaining three, and a blind solver reaches D by two form moves with no reading. Against that: the split is a by-product of the topic (a practice-abandoned-for-cause piece has exactly one harm claim to make and the distractors must therefore be functions), authentic HP items carry valence splits routinely, and lay priors genuinely do pull toward A and B, which cuts the other way. Both G-KEY solvers reached D by quoting the anchor sentence, not by shape. Non-blocking; logged so the next TYPE-001 short can consider giving one distractor a failure valence too (e.g. a wrong failure mechanism rather than a third benefit), which would close the axis at no cost to the trap architecture.

The enumeration is the batch18 supplement's RULE 13 list, not the list mech.py actually carries in this worktree, and the two differ in both directions.
findings.evidence: gates/scripts/mech.py _ABSOLUTIZERS read at source, 25 tokens: {aldrig, all, alla, allt, alltid, always, certainly, enbart, endast, entirely, every, garanterat, guarantees, helt, impossible, inga, ingen, inget, never, none, omojligt, only, proves, samtliga, varje}. The note's enumeration ADDS completely, nothing, nobody, 'no one', nowhere, everyone, everybody, everything, ingenting, ingenstans, uteslutande - none of which are in this tree's list - and OMITS none, entirely, impossible, proves, guarantees, certainly, which are. BRIEF-ADDENDUM.md efterhandstillagg item 2 records the family completion (adding nothing/nobody/no one/ingenting/ingenstans/uteslutande) as an owner ruling of 2026-08-31, but that completion is NOT present in this worktree's mech.py.
findings.why: The load-bearing conclusion survives under BOTH lists, checked both ways by this audit: mech._has_absolutizer returns False for all four options under the 25-token list actually in force, AND no option contains any token from the fuller RULE 13 family either. So M-FORM passes, no option is the lone absolutiser-free one, and the strike-the-absolutes heuristic cannot locate the key. Two separate things are recorded here and neither is item-affecting: the note describes a list that this tree does not implement, and it enumerates that list inaccurately. The item is unharmed; the process observation is that a batch supplement declared a code change that the code has not received.

findings.claim: phrase_probe_note contradicts itself inside one clause. It says the nearest neighbour of 'At that job it worked' is "'and it did' inside a longer period in a DIFFERENT unit, elf-b16-003, which reads 'and it did' nowhere either" - simultaneously locating the phrase in elf-b16-003 and denying it is there.
findings.evidence: Substring tests run by this audit over both sibling passages as shipped. batch16/candidates-final/elf-b16-003.json: 'and it did' False, 'did its job' False, 'At that job' False, 'it worked' False. batch17/candidates-final/elf-b17-003.json: identical, all four False. The phrase is in NEITHER unit, so the half of the sentence that locates it in elf-b16-003 is simply false.
findings.why: The conclusion the note is reaching for - that 'At that job it worked' is not a burned phrase and not an M-ECHO hit - is TRUE, and M-ECHO passes independently on the shipping bytes against all 114 indexed units, so nothing rests on the garbled sentence. Cosmetic self-inconsistency in an audit-facing note, the same species as elf-b17-003's scrambled key_letter_note (and worth recording that this unit's key_letter_note, the field that failed last time, is exactly right this time).

findings.claim: The rationale asserts that D 'recasts exactly that in different words ... and adds nothing the text does not supply'. D adds one thing: uptake. 'the wet it took up' asserts that the mortar absorbed the water, which the passage implies but never states.
findings.evidence: Passage, in full on this point: 'But mortar that touches timber passes damp to it, and whatever wet reached the torching sat against the battens until they decayed along its line.' The passage's verbs are passes (mortar to timber), reached (wet to torching) and sat (wet against battens). No verb of absorption or uptake by the mortar appears. Option D: 'It held the wet it took up against the battens, and the wood rotted there.' The language reviewer independently landed on the same phrase from a different direction, recording a 'mild garden path in key D, It held the wet it took up against the battens (took up against momentarily reads as a unit)'.
findings.why: Within paraphrase tolerance and not a defect in the key. 'mortar that touches timber passes damp to it' licenses the mortar as a carrier of damp, and 'whatever wet reached the torching sat against the battens' licenses the mortar as what keeps it there, so uptake is a short and forced inference rather than an import. It creates no second defensible answer - A, B and C are each falsified on stated grounds regardless - and D remains the only option with any licensing sentence. Recorded because the rationale's 'adds nothing' is a strong claim and this is the one place it is not literally true, and because two independent readers (this audit and the language review) stopped at the same three words.

cleared: KEY CORRECTNESS. Cold-solved D independently, arguing FOR all four options before rejecting any, on the anchor sentence 'But mortar that touches timber passes damp to it, and whatever wet reached the torching sat against the battens until they decayed along its line.' D is uniquely text-supported. A is falsified twice (the battens decayed rather than staying sound; the passage assigns 'the sheltering' to felt). B is both unstated and contradicted twice (nibs carry the unnailed courses; the torching went on AFTER the tiles were hung). C is falsified twice (the job is enumerated and bounded by 'At that job'; 'whatever wet reached the torching' concedes water got past). Both G-KEY legs independently solve D on the same sentence, 0 kills, 0 flags.

DISTRACTOR DEFENSIBILITY. No second defensible answer. Each distractor is refutable from the passage alone on stated grounds, and each carries a real misconception: A the reversed mechanism plus the 'shelter' surface-word borrow, B the lay adhesive theory of roof mortar, C the scope upgrade over an explicitly bounded endorsement. G-DISTRACTOR passes clean. Stress-tested B hardest, because real conservation literature does credit torching with helping fix tiles - it is still dead in the passage, which answers the holding question itself and answers it with nibs and nails.

STEM DESIGN. RULE 12 re-run from the stems sheet alone: 'What are we told about torching?' entails only that torching exists in the text and that the text says something about it. It predicates nothing about material, position, purpose, fate or effect, and it neither entails, favours nor excludes any of the four claims. The elf-b17-003 appositive misfire is not repeated. The title 'Hair and Lime' is neutral on the same test, and the rejected alternative 'Hanging by a Nib' was rightly rejected for entailing B's elimination.

EVERY DECLARED STATISTIC. Recomputed, not read: 136 mech tokens, 7 sentences [37, 4, 27, 5, 26, 25, 12], mean 19.4, sd 11.6, FRE 65.8, fk 8.9, polysyllabic 5.9 percent, paragraphs 1, prompt 6, options 16/16/15/15, ratio 1.0667 -> 1.07 against a 2.36 cap. Exact, without a single discrepancy. Every _band_check citation verified against gates/bands.json. All six mech gates re-run and pass on the shipping bytes with M-ECHO indexing the declared 114 units.

RATIONALE QUOTE FIDELITY. All six quoted strings in the rationale reproduce verbatim in the passage, and the two option-level quotes reproduce in their options. Zero stale quotes, zero invented quotes. The 'shelter' borrow the rationale attributes to option A is real (the passage's 'does the sheltering now'), so the surface_word_match label is earned and not decorative.

MECHANISM. Verified at the primary source by fetching and extracting it, not by report: the Wienerberger/Sandtoft note states that torching contact with timber battens introduces 'dampness and eventual decay' and 'goes against all current roof tiling practice and indeed British Standards', that its purpose was draughts and driving rain, and that the underlay performs those functions now. Corroborated on three further sources for nibs, fourth-course nailing, horsehair, the late-1930s underfelt displacement and the felt-under-battens geometry. The passage runs the mechanism the right way round; the batch15 backwards-mechanism failure is not repeated. The lime-conservation counter-view exists, is disclosed by the generator, and is conceded in the passage's own 'At that job it worked'.

LAW 16 / REAL-ENTITY. Re-run, not re-read. en.wiki CirrusSearch with a PASSING positive control in the same session ('Pellew' 701): 'Gimberfold' 0, 'Edith Gimberfold' 0. Quoted WebSearch: no exact bearer of either string; the control 'Robert Brindlow' returns fuzzy neighbours only, exactly reproducing the generator's honest downgrade of that instrument. Four near-variant probes added by this audit (Gimberfold, Timberfold, Gimberfield, Kimberfold) return 0 on en.wiki AND 0 on OSM Nominatim, closing the one gap the generator left - it probed variants of the name it REJECTED but not of the name it kept. 'Edith' is absent from the 231 + 14 given-name lists and from every shipped candidate file. Recommendation: lift FLAGGED-FOR-V-FINAL to CLEARED-BY-V-FINAL.

CLONE / TOPIC DISJOINTNESS. Every grep in clone_check_note reproduces: 'torching' 0 in the authentic corpus; all 133 'batten' hits are Swedish debatten-family; zero hits for torching/batten/sarking/tegelpannor/roof-tile across all shipped candidates-final. The 121-exclusion figure is exact (107 + 14) and no excluded family concerns roofs, tiles or torching - the nearest, 'tegelbrukshistoria-facktext-long', is Swedish brickworks manufacture, and the generator's manufacture-vs-fixing distinction is sound. The generator also volunteered its own unfixable overlap (practitioner byline, no quoted voice) rather than hiding it, and G-REGISTER converted that disclosure into a binding commitment on the next TYPE-001 short.

KEY LETTER. D. Sequence and tally verified by reading the eight files: C, B, B, C, D, B, A, C = A 1, B 3, C 3, D 1. The note is exactly right - notable because this is the field that was internally scrambled in elf-b17-003, and the defect did not recur.

READABILITY DEVIATION. fk 8.9 against an 11.0-15.0 authoring band is DECLARED, not hidden, and its defence is true on re-derivation across all 31 shipped ELF shorts: the spread runs 7.0 to 16.2, with the two named comparators at 7.2 and 8.7 exactly as cited. No mechanical gate checks readability; G-REGISTER passed the voice.
